comments.content: Man, there must be so much of this kind of work out there in the world and in need of automating. I really want to convince customers to use me as the centre of their tech world. I know that's a big sell but the potential of what you can build is massive when you control the center. ⁠In my first dev job, I worked in a marketing agency that basically did this for a very large multinational holiday company, and I couldn't believe how much tech they were willing to have outside of their business. What they really cared about was the results. We ended up integrating massively with their business, bringing all their data into our business, cleaning it up, merging it together and eventually they started using us as the source of truth for their media data!!! We started out doing large email broadcasts for them, that was the in, but we ended up writing software that booked people onto their seats on the airplanes and let them choose their meal and things like that. ⁠

Perfect! Yes the PRD skill, and understanding the basics of the tech you want to build products or services around is what I’d go after!

Use ai by asking tons of questions. If you want to build a web app, typescript and react is a great place to start! You can upload the typescript handbook to a GPT and have Chat GPT tasks send you lessons each morning on a timer. You can also use the fisherman prompt in the first skool module to break the topics out into step by step lessons.

That’s a nice method to PAIR with finding open source projects on github that inspire you. You clone them down to your computer and use your cursor chat to ask tons and tons of questions. How does this work? How does this connect to that? What’s that word mean? Explain like I’m 5. Explain like I’m a network engineer with XYZ skillset and make analogies to my industry.

In short + gpts trained on desired stack + OSS is a great jumping off point. Then finding a problem YOU want to solve. Then chasing that thread. It will get you through the ups and the downs. The downs are where you LEARN!

Actually I have another client that's a product distributor. It's an absolute pain making new product codes for them because different products have different specs. The product codes are stored in a table (below). Every time a new product is introduced we have to think up a way to fit the important data about the product into the existing table structure. It would be wildly helpful if...
1.) An agent could gather the necessary information and then create the product code automatically.
2.) The data could be managed in such a way that agents could store relevant data dynamically. I.e. cups have 5 spec fields, spoons have 3, so the database doesn't have a bunch of blank fields.

Hope that makes sense!
